thread.title: Midday Update: Wall Street Turns Defensive Amid Rising Mideast Tensions

author: MT Newswires
title: Midday Update: Wall Street Turns Defensive Amid Rising Mideast Tensions
text:
Shutterstock photo Wall Street's major market averages fell back into the red at midday as Wall Street braces for a speech from the Israeli prime minister that could re-ignite the conflict in the Mideast, and profit-taking pressure on the technology sector. Led by Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Celgene ( CELG ), the Nasdaq Composite surrendered its early gains and is underpforming its peers.
Stocks were gaining altitude on Monday with a barrage of mergers and upbeat earnings fueling Monday's positive price action. Led by gains in component stocks McDonald's ( MCD ) and Apple ( AAPL ), the blue chip index was trading with a triple-digit gain.
Higher Treasury yields and the surging dollar took a backseat to a flood M&A activity over the weekend and strong quarterly results from McDonald's and Allergan ( AGN ). Although the headlines were dominated by Sprint's (S) merger with T-Mobile (TMUS), several other multi-billion dollar deals also hit the tape before Monday's open including a $35.6 billion acquisition of Andeavor (ANDV) by Marathon (MRO), and Marriott Vacation's (VAC) acquisition of ILG (ILG).
Ahead of a very busy week on the economic front, the first round of data indicated solid growth with personal income and spending up 0.3% and 0.4%, respectively, and the Chicago PMI improving to 57.6 in April from 57.4 previously, though slightly missing estimates of 57.8.
A miss on the pending home sales index (+0.4% vs +1.0% estimates) coupled with reports that Israel closed its airspace with Syria prompted the first pull-back in stocks. Shares retreated for a second time amid headlines that Israel prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu will make a "significant" announcement on Iran showing the country cheated on its nuclear deal with the U.S.
European shares held modest gains and ended the month with its best performance since September despite soft German retail sales. Germany's DAX outperformed its EU peers while the UK's FTSE-100 lagged with investors spooked after the House of Lords voted in favor of extra parliamentary powers over Brexit.
Crude oil was up $0.17 to $68.34 per barrel. Natural gas was down $0.04 to $2.73 per 1 million BTU. Gold was down $5.60 to $1,317.70 an ounce, while silver was down $0.12 to $16.37 an ounce. Copper was down $0.004 to $3.06 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was up 0.51% to $13.80 with the United States Natural Gas Fund was down 1.24% to $22.32. Amongst precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was down 1.71% to 22.32 while SPDR Gold Shares were down 0.51% to $124.86. The iShares Silver Trust was down 1.06% to $15.40.
